result.response:
All 9 tests pass. Three independent source bugs, each fixed at the root:

**1. `packages/cli/src/flags.js`** — numeric flag values were left as strings (the code even had a `TODO: numbers stay strings` marker). Now pure-numeric values are coerced with `/^\d+$/.test(next) ? Number(next) : next`, so `--port 8080` yields the number `8080`. Non-numeric values (`--host example.com`) and bare flags (`--verbose` → `true`) are unaffected.

**2. `packages/shared/src/dates.js`** — `dayKey` was documented as grouping "by calendar day in UTC" but used local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`). The test sets `TZ=America/New_York`, so `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` crossed midnight back to `2026-01-01`. Switched to `getUTCFullYear`/`getUTCMonth`/`getUTCDate`.

**3. `packages/shared/src/format.js`** — `displayName` dereferenced `user.name` with no guard, throwing `Cannot read properties of null` for `displayName(null)`. Now uses optional chaining and returns `"anonymous"` for `null`, `{}`, or a blank/whitespace-only name, while still trimming `"  Ada Lovelace "` → `"Ada Lovelace"`.

Verified beyond the suite: `parseFlags` still handles mixed args correctly, and `npm run bench` runs clean (200k lines, 529 ms). No changes to the tests themselves — all three were legitimate assertions of intended behavior.

All three bugs are in the source, and the tests define intended behavior:

All 9 tests pass. There were three separate bugs:

**1. `packages/cli/src/flags.js` — port stayed a string**
`parseFlags` stored raw argv values, so `--port 8080` yielded `'8080'` (there was even a `TODO: numbers stay strings`). Now all-digit values are coerced with `Number(next)`; string flags like `--verbose` still become `true`.

**2. `packages/shared/src/dates.js` — day keys used local time**
`dayKey` used `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate` (local timezone), but the contract (per the comment and test, which sets `TZ=America/New_York`) is UTC day grouping — `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` is still Jan 1 in New York. Switched to the `getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate` variants.

**3. `packages/shared/src/format.js` — no null guard**
`displayName` did `user.name.trim()` and crashed on `null`/`{}`. Now returns the trimmed name when present, falling back to `"anonymous"`.

Also verified the only other consumer, `src/index.js`, passes `flags.port` to `listen()` — a numeric port works fine there.

data.delta:
All 9 tests pass. Three independent source bugs, each fixed at the root:

**1. `packages/cli/src/flags.js`** — numeric flag values were left as strings (the code even had a `TODO: numbers stay strings` marker). Now pure-numeric values are coerced with `/^\d+$/.test(next) ? Number(next) : next`, so `--port 8080` yields the number `8080`. Non-numeric values (`--host example.com`) and bare flags (`--verbose` → `true`) are unaffected.

**2. `packages/shared/src/dates.js`** — `dayKey` was documented as grouping "by calendar day in UTC" but used local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`). The test sets `TZ=America/New_York`, so `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` crossed midnight back to `2026-01-01`. Switched to `getUTCFullYear`/`getUTCMonth`/`getUTCDate`.

**3. `packages/shared/src/format.js`** — `displayName` dereferenced `user.name` with no guard, throwing `Cannot read properties of null` for `displayName(null)`. Now uses optional chaining and returns `"anonymous"` for `null`, `{}`, or a blank/whitespace-only name, while still trimming `"  Ada Lovelace "` → `"Ada Lovelace"`.

Verified beyond the suite: `parseFlags` still handles mixed args correctly, and `npm run bench` runs clean (200k lines, 529 ms). No changes to the tests themselves — all three were legitimate assertions of intended behavior.

All 9 tests pass. There were three separate bugs:

**1. `packages/cli/src/flags.js` — port stayed a string**
`parseFlags` stored raw argv values, so `--port 8080` yielded `'8080'` (there was even a `TODO: numbers stay strings`). Now all-digit values are coerced with `Number(next)`; string flags like `--verbose` still become `true`.

**2. `packages/shared/src/dates.js` — day keys used local time**
`dayKey` used `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate` (local timezone), but the contract (per the comment and test, which sets `TZ=America/New_York`) is UTC day grouping — `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` is still Jan 1 in New York. Switched to the `getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate` variants.

**3. `packages/shared/src/format.js` — no null guard**
`displayName` did `user.name.trim()` and crashed on `null`/`{}`. Now returns the trimmed name when present, falling back to `"anonymous"`.

Also verified the only other consumer, `src/index.js`, passes `flags.port` to `listen()` — a numeric port works fine there.

Fixed. `npm test` now passes **9/9** (was 6/9), and `npm run bench` still works.

**Root causes and fixes** (each bug was flagged by a TODO in its file):

1. **`[cli-flag]`** — `packages/cli/src/flags.js`: flag values were stored as strings, so `--port 8080` gave `'8080'` instead of `8080`. Now pure-digit values are converted with `Number` (same `/^\d+$/` convention the repo uses in `bench/parse.js`).
2. **`[timezone]`** — `packages/shared/src/dates.js`: `dayKey` used local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`) although its doc says day keys are UTC days; with `TZ=America/New_York`, `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` produced `2026-01-01`. Switched to `getUTCFullYear`/`getUTCMonth`/`getUTCDate`.
3. **`[null-guard]`** — `packages/shared/src/format.js`: `displayName` dereferenced `user.name` and threw on `null`. Now `user?.name?.trim()` with `"anonymous"` fallback for `null`, `{}`, and whitespace-only names.

Notes:
- The `edit` skill was unavailable in this kernel, so I applied the same exact unique-match string replacements via Python.
- I also updated the stale README line that said "Three tests fail on purpose".
- No dependencies needed installing: `node --test` (Node v22.23.4) doesn't import `kleur`/`ms`, which are only used by `src/index.js` at runtime.

}
